archived_by: repo hygiene — Profile B residual archive (git slim plan)

residual_findings.title: clippy allow(clippy::unwrap_used) on cron test module lacked justification comment
residual_findings.note: Repo AGENTS.md mandates a brief justification comment on every #[allow(...)].
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: added justification comment 'test-only — .unwrap() keeps assertion intent readable; panics surface test names.'

residual_findings.title: existing_canonical_names read failure produced zero candidates with no warn! trail
residual_findings.note: Errors ARE propagated via '?', but the supervisor hook treats extraction as best-effort and does not fail the terminal transition. A flaky kb_key_blocks read silently produced zero candidates with no warn! trail at the orchestration layer.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: rewrote the error arm as an explicit match that logs at warn! before propagating. The warn names the world_id, the underlying error, and explicitly notes that the terminal transition still completes (best-effort contract preserved).

residual_findings.title: Conflicting flags (--role EXPR --no-role) silently last-write-wins
residual_findings.note: Pre-fix: --brainstorm '0 9 * * *' --no-brainstorm stored the cron expression on a role whose enabled=false. Authors reading the schedule back see the cron string attached to a disabled role.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: pre-mutation conflict check in apply_set_args rejects the (brainstorm, write, review) self-contradictions with stable code E_CRON_CONFLICTING_FLAGS. Hermetic test apply_set_args_conflicting_role_flags_rejected_with_stable_code covers all three pairs.

residual_findings.title: clippy allow(clippy::too_many_arguments) on handle_advance lacked justification comment
residual_findings.note: Sibling perform_advance in nexus-orchestration/src/auto_chronology.rs already carried the model comment; this site was missed during T-A P3 fix-wave.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: added justification mirroring the sibling perform_advance comment ('the 8 inputs are read together from one CLI invocation + one Work row; packing them into a struct would duplicate the WorkAutoChronologyRow shape').

residual_findings.title: resolve_work_id_by_ref_or_id used LIMIT 1 without ORDER BY (non-deterministic on collision)
residual_findings.note: In the theoretical case where a work_ref slug collides with another row's work_id, the chosen row was non-deterministic and might disagree with the 'ref wins over id' precedence the doc comment promises.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: added ORDER BY work_ref IS NULL, work_id to the SELECT. Hermetic test resolve_work_id_by_ref_or_id_prefers_work_ref_match_on_collision seeds a deliberate collision and asserts work_ref wins.

residual_findings.title: CRON_SCHEDULE_CACHE / CRON_PARSE_COUNT process-globals had no test-isolation contract doc
residual_findings.note: Statics are shared across every test in the same binary. Mitigations hold today (per-binary process boundary; only one lib test reads CRON_PARSE_COUNT; integration tests use unique work_ids). Design is fragile to future test additions.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: added explicit test-isolation contract doc to both statics enumerating the three current mitigations and explicitly forbidding future tests from asserting on CRON_PARSE_COUNT from tests/ or reusing existing test work_ids (would regress to an R-V149P1-02-style flake).

residual_findings.title: list --json output omitted work_id (work_ref:null left row unidentifiable)
residual_findings.note: JSON path emitted {work_ref, schedule} but not work_id. A Work with work_ref = null produced {"work_ref": null, ...} with no identifier for machine consumers.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: extracted JSON-row construction into pure helper list_row_to_json; emits {work_ref, work_id, schedule}. Hermetic test list_row_to_json_includes_work_id_and_work_ref covers both cases (with slug + null slug).

residual_findings.title: Idempotency-check error path skipped CronFireSummary counter
residual_findings.note: Err arm only logged at warn! and did not touch the summary; a Work whose idempotency check errored was silently absent from CronFireSummary::total_evaluated().
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: added dedicated summary bucket 'skipped_idempotency_check_error' (separate from skipped_idempotent so operators can spot a flaky reads path); incremented in the Err arm; surfaced in the 'sweep complete' log line. Contract test summary_total_evaluated_includes_idempotency_check_error_bucket covers the arithmetic.

residual_findings.title: set_schedule_json_tx rationale prose was internally contradictory
residual_findings.note: Doc first called the daemon-side cron evaluator 'the racing party' against the CLI writer, then admitted the evaluator 'does not write schedule_json'. The actual race is between two concurrent CLI invocations or future daemon-side mutators (e.g. T-A P3 auto-chronology).
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 P-last T2: reworded the doc comment to match reality (the CAS protects against concurrent CLI invocations + future daemon-side mutators; the T-A P1 cron evaluator is read-only on this column).
